parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with payroll, so the module does serve one concern. The problem is that its two files reach data in different ways. PayrollService always goes through domain repositories (EmployeeRepository, TimesheetRepository), turns rows into model objects (Employee, Timesheet, Payslip) and throws model errors. PayrollAuditService skips that repository layer: it takes the raw PrismaService and calls ORM methods directly (prisma.payrollAudit.create and findMany). It also builds persistence details itself: a record id from `${Date.now()}-${subject}` and an `at` timestamp. And it maps ORM rows into an AuditLine interface declared in the service file, not in src/business/model. So the module has no single consistent abstraction or boundary. One service works through repositories and domain models; the other is a thin wrapper over the ORM. That is a bypass of the abstraction the module otherwise uses. Which way the imports point is out of scope. This finding is only about the module mixing abstraction levels.

violations.message: PayrollAuditService skips the repository and domain-model abstraction that the rest of the module uses (PayrollService goes through EmployeeRepository/TimesheetRepository and model classes). It injects PrismaService and calls prisma.payrollAudit.create/findMany directly, builds record ids and timestamps itself, and declares its own AuditLine shape. This mixes abstraction levels within the module.
